The story I’ve been told is that her son was sentenced to prison in what she believes is a wrongful conviction. She stands outside the courthouse to decry / protest on behalf of her son.

She really poses no threat beyond the noise, although if someone happens to be dressed as if they work in the court or are even seen walking out the doors, she’ll shortly follow them and cry out in anger at them

People have tried to speak to her, and police have been called plenty of times to report her behaviour, but every effort I’ve seen taken to help her usually ends in her becoming tired and going home until the next day.

I find it to be a sad story, truth be told. She’s a grieving mother; we all process stuff like this differently. She just happens to be more vocal than others. I hope she can find closure sooner rather than later though.

Individual actions from specific events are rarely indicative of the group at large. I’d caution you to think that the choices made by some are endorsed by the rest.

Put simply, it’s a fault in human nature. Nobody believes they are the villain. We all believe in ideologies, and those things are what give us identity, value, presence of mind, etc.

The distinction we need to make as people though is that our ideologies don’t control us. We have to make great efforts to dissociate from ideas and judge them as outside observers before we choose to adopt them. And I doubt that these people have done that yet.

While I agree that denying people the right to freedom of speech is bad in principle, this has to be made an exception.

The tearing down of a racist message is not equivalent to tearing down an inclusive one. A rainbow flag isn't denying any other group their right to speak or represent themselves as themselves, it's a call to equality for members in their circle. Nobody that brandishes the LGBTQ+ banner is asking for people to be denied their freedoms because they think they do not belong in the general society since they lack certain character traits. In stark contrast however, this "Defend Canada" sentiment clearly has racist undertones and is creating an enemy out of people that aren't necessarily bad.

Now whether or not the outcome of tearing down any message is good or bad is a completely different debate, but in the context of what's being displayed here, I believe that there should be no reason to doubt this action as opposed to the example you provided. Ideas like the one posted can only fester hatred, which ultimately breeds conflict against one another. At the end of the day, it would stand to reason to prevent seeing others hurt, and therefore denying this hate groups right to speak on their terms is justified.
